remaining_uncertainties: Forward citations: 7 seeds were retrieved (KYC 28 citing works, 2512.02902 17, LIBERO-RIG 1, CMA 1, RSB 1, 2610.01626 0, More Structure 0/empty). The More Structure gap is closed to medium-high confidence only: its empty list was returned three times with HTTP 200, but in the same session RSB first returned an empty list and later returned 1, so S2 evidently emits transient empty 200 responses. Google Scholar's exact-title query shows no 'Cited by' entry for More Structure (the same query returns 22 for KYC), which is the second independent channel.

OpenAlex single-work cited_by_count is not usable as citation evidence for these arXiv DOIs: it returns 0 for KYC, which has 22-28 citing works in Scholar/S2. Earlier passes cited it as corroboration; that reasoning is corrected in the report and self-audit.

The surviving candidate C1 was narrowed again in pass 7. Two new competing explanations were identified from published cells (LIT Table II): (a) a generic interface fix improves all perturbation axes on the real robot (+16.7/+16.7/+13.3), so failure-mode specificity is not a general law; (b) gain tracks headroom (1 - baseline) across architectures (+27.43 at 16.40 vs +2.39 at 82.16), so a failure-composition predictor may merely restate headroom. C1 must beat a headroom null model on held-out tasks, and there is still no pilot evidence that same-task/different-failure-mode variants can be constructed.

None of the four papers whose protocols C1 would reuse (More Structure, LIBERO-RIG, 2610.01626, 2512.02902) contains a project or code URL; the failure taxonomy and tolerance protocol must be reimplemented (unverified 1-2 week cost). By contrast, the closest interface-modification competitor (LIT 2609.12641) publishes Apache-2.0 code, Hugging Face checkpoints and real-robot data, so the reproducible half of this literature is the half where novelty is exhausted.
42 of 101 registered papers were read at abstract level only (arXiv HTML rate limits); they may contain direct competitors that would change the crowding judgement.
Conference-versus-arXiv version differences were not compared for most entries.

Real-robot evidence in this literature rests on 20-30 trials per condition (LIT: 25 ID / 10 OOD rollouts per task), which limits the statistical strength of any action-level claim, including future ones.
Whether a measurement/prediction contribution is acceptable as the master's small paper is an advisor judgement that literature research cannot settle.
conclusion: After 136 recorded arXiv queries (eight rounds, 2,480 unique records), seven forward-citation seeds and 101 registered papers, five of seven directions fail the hard vetoes. A pass-7 integrity audit re-verified all 101 arXiv IDs by title (101/101), closed the More Structure citation gap (S2 empty; Scholar shows no 'Cited by' where the same query returns 22 for KYC), and corrected a faulty inference that had treated OpenAlex's zero count as corroboration. The audit also surfaced one unregistered full text (LIT, 2609.12641) that is a direct competitor to C2 and a two-sided competitor to C1: its generic interface fix improves every perturbation axis on the real robot, and its per-architecture gains track headroom. One direction therefore survives only in a narrowed, medium-low-confidence form: whether baseline failure-mode composition plus the intervention's reduction of the operative spatial error predicts the action benefit of a spatial upgrade, beyond what a headroom model explains. The report recommends no experiment until seven explicit gates are met (gate 4 now requires equal data budget for the alignment control; gate 5 now requires beating Delta_hat = alpha*(1-baseline)), and states that if the predictive relation does not hold, no candidate in this scope qualifies.
